heart_attack.title: Heart Attack (Myocardial Infarction)
steps: Call 108 (ambulance) or 112 immediately
Have the person sit down and rest in a comfortable position (usually semi-upright)
If the person is not allergic, give them an aspirin (325mg) to chew slowly
Loosen any tight clothing
If the person becomes unconscious and stops breathing, begin CPR
If an AED is available, use it following the device instructions
Stay with the person until emergency services arrive
Do NOT leave the person alone, Do NOT give them anything other than aspirin
doNot: Do not let the person walk or exert themselves
Do not ignore symptoms even if they seem mild
Do not delay calling emergency services

stroke.title: Stroke
steps: Use FAST method: Face drooping, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty, Time to call 112
Call 108/112 immediately — every minute matters
Note the time when symptoms first appeared
Help the person lie down with head and shoulders slightly elevated
Do NOT give them food, water, or medication
If the person is unconscious, place them in recovery position
If vomiting, turn head to the side to prevent choking
Be prepared to perform CPR if they stop breathing
doNot: Do not give aspirin (could be hemorrhagic stroke)
Do not give any food or drink
Do not let them go to sleep

choking.title: Choking
steps: Ask 'Are you choking?' — if they cannot speak, act immediately
Stand behind the person, wrap your arms around their waist
Make a fist with one hand, place it above the navel
Grasp your fist with other hand and thrust inward and upward (Heimlich maneuver)
Repeat until object is expelled or person becomes unconscious
If unconscious, lower them to ground and begin CPR
Look in mouth before giving breaths — remove visible object
Call 112 if object is not expelled quickly
doNot: Do not slap the back if the person can still cough
Do not try to reach into throat blindly
Do not give water

severe_bleeding.title: Severe Bleeding
steps: Call 108/112 for severe bleeding
Apply firm, direct pressure to the wound with a clean cloth
If possible, elevate the injured area above the heart
Do NOT remove the cloth if blood soaks through — add more layers on top
Apply pressure continuously for at least 15 minutes
If bleeding is from a limb and won't stop, apply a tourniquet above the wound
Keep the person warm and lying down (shock prevention)
Monitor breathing and consciousness until help arrives
doNot: Do not remove embedded objects
Do not apply a tourniquet around neck or torso
Do not use a tourniquet unless bleeding is life-threatening

burns.title: Burns
steps: Remove the person from the source of burn
For minor burns: Cool under running cool (not cold) water for 10-20 minutes
Remove rings, watches, or tight items from the burned area before swelling
Cover the burn loosely with a sterile, non-stick bandage
Give over-the-counter pain relief if needed
For severe burns (large area, face, hands, genitals): Call 108/112
Cover with clean sheet while waiting for help
Monitor for signs of shock
doNot: Do not apply ice directly
Do not use butter, toothpaste, or cream on burns
Do not break blisters
Do not remove clothing stuck to the burn

fracture.title: Bone Fracture
steps: Keep the person still — do not move the injured area
Call for medical help or go to ER
Immobilize the injury in the position found — use splint if available
Apply ice wrapped in cloth (not directly) to reduce swelling
For open fractures (bone visible): Cover wound with sterile dressing, call 108
Treat for shock if needed: lay flat, elevate legs, keep warm
Do NOT try to realign the bone
Monitor circulation below the injury (pulse, sensation, skin color)
doNot: Do not try to straighten the bone
Do not move the person if spine injury is suspected
Do not apply heat

seizure.title: Seizure / Epileptic Episode
steps: Stay calm and time the seizure
Clear the area of hard or sharp objects
Place something soft under their head
Turn them onto their side (recovery position) to prevent choking
Do NOT restrain the person or put anything in their mouth
Stay with them until they are fully conscious
Call 108/112 if: seizure lasts >5 minutes, person doesn't wake up, it's their first seizure, or they are pregnant
After seizure, speak calmly and help them orient
doNot: Do not hold them down
Do not put anything in their mouth
Do not give food/water until fully alert

allergic_reaction.title: Severe Allergic Reaction (Anaphylaxis)
steps: Call 108/112 immediately — anaphylaxis is life-threatening
If the person has an EpiPen, help them use it (inject into outer thigh)
Help them lie down with legs elevated (unless breathing is difficult)
If breathing is difficult, let them sit up
Loosen tight clothing
If they stop breathing, begin CPR
A second dose of epinephrine can be given after 5-15 minutes if no improvement
Even if symptoms improve, they must go to ER (biphasic reactions can occur)
doNot: Do not give oral medication if they're having trouble swallowing
Do not leave them alone
Do not assume symptoms will resolve on their own

heatstroke.title: Heatstroke
steps: Call 108/112 immediately
Move the person to a cool, shaded area
Remove excess clothing
Cool the body rapidly: apply cold water/ice packs to neck, armpits, groin
Fan the person while misting with cool water
If conscious, give small sips of cool water
Do NOT give aspirin or acetaminophen for heatstroke
Monitor body temperature and continue cooling until it drops to 101°F/38.3°C
doNot: Do not give large amounts of water at once
Do not use rubbing alcohol to cool
Do not give fever-reducing medications

poisoning.title: Poisoning
steps: Call Poison Information Centre: 011-2658-9391 or dial 112
Try to identify what was ingested, how much, and when
Do NOT induce vomiting unless instructed by poison control
If the poison is on the skin, remove contaminated clothing and rinse with water for 20 minutes
If in the eyes, rinse with clean water for 15-20 minutes
If inhaled, move to fresh air immediately
Save the container/substance for identification
If unconscious, place in recovery position and monitor breathing
doNot: Do not induce vomiting (especially for corrosive/petroleum products)
Do not give activated charcoal without medical advice
Do not give food or drink

diabetic_emergency.title: Diabetic Emergency (Hypo/Hyperglycemia)
steps: If conscious and able to swallow: give sugar — juice, candy, glucose tablets
If symptoms suggest LOW sugar (shaking, sweating, confusion): give sugar immediately
If symptoms suggest HIGH sugar (fruity breath, excessive thirst, frequent urination): do NOT give sugar
If unsure whether high or low, give sugar — low sugar is more immediately dangerous
Check blood glucose if meter is available
If person is unconscious, call 108/112 immediately
Place unconscious person in recovery position
Do NOT give insulin unless you are trained and it's prescribed
doNot: Do not give food/drink to unconscious person
Do not administer insulin without proper knowledge
Do not ignore symptoms

drowning.title: Drowning / Near-Drowning
steps: Call 108/112 immediately
Remove person from water (ensure your own safety first)
Check for breathing — if not breathing, begin CPR immediately
If no pulse, continue with chest compressions and rescue breaths
If person is breathing, place in recovery position
Remove wet clothing and keep them warm
Even if the person seems fine, they MUST go to hospital (secondary drowning)
Monitor continuously until help arrives
doNot: Do not attempt a water rescue unless trained
Do not assume they are fine just because they are conscious
Do not give up CPR
